```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Azure Database for PostgreSQL hosts a PostgreSQL database for you. With
shinyOAuthDB, people sign in to your Shiny app with their Microsoft account
and query data using the permissions already assigned to them in PostgreSQL.

The database maps their Microsoft identity to a database role: a user or
group with permission to read particular data. `oauth_db_azure_postgres()`
opens an RPostgres connection for that role, which you can use with DBI or
dbplyr.

## Try the guided demo

Run `shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_cloud_demo("azure-postgres")` in the R console
for an editable app that walks through setup. In addition to RPostgres,
install `bslib`, `processx` and `askpass` for the local app.

The launcher asks for your Azure server, database role and sign-in settings.
After signing in, click **Run example query** to see the connected database
and role. It uses your existing Azure server; stopping the app leaves that
server running. See `?oauth_db_cloud_demo` for optional settings and
[Getting started](getting-started.html#more-ways-to-try-an-app) for editing
and resuming demos.

## Set up access

In R, run `install.packages("RPostgres")`. Ask your administrator to
[enable Entra authentication and create database roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/security/security-entra-configure)
for the app's users or their groups. You'll need the server and database
names, the database role to connect as, and a certificate bundle for the server.

Create an Entra Web app registration for PostgreSQL access and register
`http://localhost:8100` as its redirect URI. Save these values in a local
`.Renviron` file and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID=your-tenant-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
```

Use the [Microsoft registration steps](azure-sql.html#register-a-microsoft-entra-app)
and configure delegated access to **Azure OSSRDBMS Database**. The client
preset requests the appropriate PostgreSQL permissions; see
`?oauth_db_microsoft_client` when combining it with other services.

| Value in the app | Where to find it |
| --- | --- |
| `host` | Azure PostgreSQL server overview, full server name ending in `.postgres.database.azure.com` |
| `dbname` | The database name in your existing connection settings |
| `user` | The Entra user or group role created in PostgreSQL by the Entra administrator |
| `sslrootcert` | The CA bundle recommended for your server's certificate chain |
| Tenant ID, client ID, secret | [Entra registration](azure-sql.html#register-a-microsoft-entra-app) |

Allow the app host through the server's networking settings too.

## A complete app

Save this as `example.R`. Replace the host, database, and role name, and set
`sslrootcert` to your CA bundle's path:

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_microsoft_client(
  services = "postgres",
  tenant_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID"),
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_azure_postgres(
    auth$connection,
    host = "example.postgres.database.azure.com",
    dbname = "reporting",
    user = "reporting-readers",
    sslrootcert = "path/to/root-ca.pem"
  )

  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT current_user")
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*"),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at http://localhost:8100
# (viewers in RStudio/Positron/etc. cannot perform necessary redirects)
```

Run `source("example.R")` and open
`http://localhost:8100`. Sign in to run the query; signing out clears the
output.

## Read a table

The first query shows the PostgreSQL role. To read your data, replace that
output expression with a query for your table:

```{r table-query}
output$rows <- renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT * FROM reporting.orders LIMIT 20")
})
```

Call `con()` inside the reactive expression before querying. You can also
pass the resulting `connection` to `dplyr::tbl()` for dbplyr queries.
Use DBI parameter binding for SQL values entered by users.

## Create the database identity

In Azure PostgreSQL's **Authentication** settings, enable Entra and set an
Entra administrator. That administrator creates the database principals
for the people or groups who will use the app. Azure provides
`pgaadauth_create_principal` for this; its [Entra setup guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/security/security-entra-configure)
shows the supported commands and group mapping. Grant the resulting role
database/schema access and SELECT on the intended tables.

Use that exact database role as `user` in the app. The example's shared
group role assumes the server maps signed-in members to that group. With
individual roles, choose a role for the current identity and have the
server verify the mapping; don't let arbitrary input choose another role.

## Roles and connection settings

You can omit `sslrootcert` if libpq already has the correct CA bundle
configured. Other options, such as `port` and `connect_timeout`, go to
RPostgres. See `?oauth_db_azure_postgres` for the connection arguments.

Use RPostgres linked to libpq 16 or later. The helper requires the server
to request the visitor's access token as its password over verified TLS;
Kerberos, certificate-only and trust authentication cannot replace it.
Authentication and TLS settings cannot be changed through `...`.

For custom sign-in settings or saved query results, see
[Getting started](getting-started.html#sessions-saved-results-and-extra-permissions).
